status_summary: BIS funding rose: its FY2026 congressional budget submission requested 303.0 million dollars and 830 positions against 191.0 million and 585 positions enacted for FY2024, and the FY2026 appropriations law signed 2026-01-23 (Public Law 119-74) provided 235.0 million, 23 percent above FY2025 but 68 million below the request. For FY2027, the Under Secretary told the House Foreign Affairs Committee on 2026-07-14 that BIS seeks 301 million dollars for export enforcement against 122 million in FY2026, with enforcement positions rising from 299 to 669; the testimony does not mention the intelligence community, SCIFs, clearances or CFIUS. Division F of Public Law 119-60 (signed 2025-12-18) requires the DNI to support and consult with CFIUS and the FBI when they review acquisitions of entities holding biological data by foreign entities of concern, a standing duty in effect since enactment, with a briefing on a formal support process due in 90 days (Sec. 6614); directs a DNI plan, to be carried out, for sharing intelligence on foreign adversary biotechnology threats with other agencies and private-sector partners (Sec. 6612); and directs the DNI to develop, within 60 days, a strategy for coordinating intelligence on critical and emerging technologies and sharing it with agencies including those handling export controls (Sec. 6623). The Senate intelligence committee's FY2027 bill reported 2026-05-20 (S. 4615, Sec. 606) would have the DNI, through the NCSC Director, seek to establish an IC counterintelligence office at Commerce headquarters with secure connectivity by 2028; it is not enacted. ODNI's page for its Office of Economic Security and Emerging Technologies says that office's Investment Security Group leads IC analysis supporting CFIUS and assesses information and services for Commerce. No published DNI strategy under Sec. 6623, SCIF expansion for BIS, or clearance program for private-sector experts was found.

timeline.event: Commerce's FY2026 congressional budget submission for BIS requested 303.0 million dollars and 830 positions, against 191.0 million and 585 positions for FY2024 (the document is undated; month taken from the file path). It names the intelligence community among interagency partners but does not mention SCIFs or clearances.

Public Law 119-60 was signed; Division F requires the DNI to support and consult with CFIUS and the FBI when they review acquisitions of entities holding biological data by foreign entities of concern, a standing duty with a briefing on a formal support process due in 90 days (Sec. 6614); directs a DNI plan, to be carried out, for sharing intelligence on foreign adversary biotechnology threats with other agencies and private-sector partners (Sec. 6612); and directs a DNI strategy within 60 days for coordinating and sharing intelligence on critical and emerging technologies with agencies including those handling export controls (Sec. 6623).
The FY2026 Commerce, Justice, Science appropriations act was signed as Public Law 119-74, providing 235.0 million dollars for BIS.

A senator wrote to the Under Secretary for Industry and Security asking about open-source and commercial tools for export-control enforcement; the letter says BIS lacks access to key commercial and government data and does not mention the intelligence community or classified systems.

The Senate intelligence committee reported S. 4615, whose Sec. 606 would have the DNI, acting through the NCSC Director, seek agreement with Commerce to establish an IC counterintelligence office in the Office of the Secretary by 2028, with DNI-funded secure facilities and connectivity.

The Under Secretary for Industry and Security testified to the House Foreign Affairs Committee that the FY2027 request would raise BIS export enforcement funding from 122 million to 301 million dollars and enforcement positions from 299 to 669; the testimony does not mention the intelligence community, SCIFs, clearances or CFIUS.

title: More intelligence support, coordination and SCIF capacity for BIS and CFIUS
uncertainties: Stage credit rests on two operative steps that carry out parts of the text. First, the enacted FY2026 BIS increase: the text lists the resources needed for BIS among the things the DNI and Commerce Secretary should increase, though the increase is not shown to fund intelligence support. Second, the Sec. 6614 standing duty for the DNI to support and consult with CFIUS on acquisitions involving biological data, which covers one sector and adds to existing ODNI analytic support for CFIUS. Rule applied: an operative step carrying out part of the text is in_progress; the Sec. 6612 plan and Sec. 6623 strategy are directives whose delivery is not public and would alone be proposed-level, and the FY2027 request and S. 4615 Sec. 606 are proposals. Judgment: a reader who treats general BIS funding as parallel to the intelligence-focused text would still have Sec. 6614 as an operative CFIUS element, so in_progress at the low end of the band is favored. The budget submission is undated; its date comes from the file path. The CRS report was read through its first 100 thousand characters. The ODNI office page is undated and does not show when its CFIUS support began, which may predate 2025. S. 4615 is a committee-reported bill; its Senate floor status was not checked. No ODNI-BIS or CFIUS clearance or SCIF arrangement was found; such arrangements may be classified.
